title: CDSS Atlas — Everyday Common Conditions Knowledge Base
purpose: A cautious, clinician-reviewable reference layer for patient-friendly explanations and follow-up questions. It is not a diagnostic model and must not force common conditions to the top.
important_rules: Never assign or invent percentages, probabilities, confidence scores, or prevalence-based boosts from this file.
A symptom pattern is not enough to confirm a disease. Present entries as possibilities only when supported by the complete case and validated logic.
Fever alone must never be labelled 'viral fever' as a confirmed cause. Use 'fever — cause not yet clear' when evidence is insufficient.
Do not suppress serious possibilities or warning signs just because a common condition matches.
Run clinically reviewed safety/triage rules before displaying routine self-care guidance.
Treat not-reported, not-asked, denied, and confirmed-absent as different states.
Negation, age, pregnancy, immune suppression, chronic conditions, duration, severity, and worsening symptoms can change the appropriate next step.
Do not recommend prescription drugs, antibiotics, or individualized doses from this knowledge base.
Do not use an entry as a standalone rule-based diagnosis; have qualified clinicians review the dataset and thresholds before patient-facing use.
general_safety_signs: Severe difficulty breathing, blue/grey lips, or inability to speak normally due to breathlessness
New confusion, collapse, seizure, or difficulty waking
Severe dehydration, inability to keep fluids down, or markedly reduced urination
Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or bleeding
Rapid worsening or a person appearing seriously unwell
Fever in a very young infant, or fever in a person who is pregnant, immunocompromised, elderly, or has significant chronic illness requires appropriate clinical guidance

general_patient_copy.uncertain_result_title: We can't tell the exact cause from these symptoms alone
general_patient_copy.uncertain_result_body: Several conditions can cause similar symptoms. We'll help you review important details and decide what to do next, but this tool cannot confirm a diagnosis.
general_patient_copy.score_label_policy: Do not display numerical disease-match percentages unless they are statistically calibrated, validated for the intended population, and clearly explained. A cosine similarity or model score is not a disease probability.
general_patient_copy.urgent_copy_policy: Urgency wording must come from a clinically reviewed triage protocol, not from the condition list or model rank.

conditions.plain_language: A common viral infection affecting the nose and throat. Symptoms are often mild, but other illnesses can look similar.
useful_follow_up_questions: When did symptoms start?
Is the main problem a runny/blocked nose or a sudden fever and strong body aches?
Any trouble breathing, dehydration, or symptoms getting worse?
Is the person an infant, older adult, pregnant, immunocompromised, or living with a significant chronic condition?
do_not_assume: A cold is not confirmed from fever alone.
Flu, COVID-19, RSV, allergies, and other conditions may overlap.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: seek professional advice if symptoms are severe, persistent, or worsening
red_flags_or_escalation: Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, dehydration, fever lasting more than several days, symptoms that fail to improve, or symptoms that improve and then worsen.

conditions.plain_language: Flu can cause a sudden illness with fever or chills, body aches, cough, headache, and marked tiredness. Symptoms overlap with other infections.
useful_follow_up_questions: Did symptoms begin suddenly?
How long have symptoms been present?
Any breathing difficulty or chest pain?
Any pregnancy, older age, immune suppression, or chronic illness?
Has a flu test or clinician assessment been done?
do_not_assume: Symptoms alone cannot reliably distinguish flu from COVID-19 or other respiratory infections.
Not everyone with flu has fever.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: reduce contact with others while ill
prompt clinical advice for people at higher risk because antiviral treatment can be time-sensitive
red_flags_or_escalation: Prompt clinical advice if high risk, very unwell, short of breath, or symptoms are not improving.

references.title: CDC — Signs and Symptoms of Flu

conditions.plain_language: COVID-19 can cause cold-like symptoms, fever, cough, tiredness, body aches, or stomach symptoms. A test may be needed to distinguish it from other illnesses.
useful_follow_up_questions: When did symptoms begin?
Any known exposure or test result?
Any breathing difficulty or chest pain?
Does the person have risk factors for severe illness?
do_not_assume: Symptoms vary and overlap with flu and common cold.
A symptom list cannot confirm COVID-19.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: consider testing according to local guidance and risk
seek prompt advice if at higher risk
red_flags_or_escalation: Use general safety signs, especially severe breathing difficulty, persistent chest pain, new confusion, or rapid worsening.

conditions.display_name: RSV or another respiratory virus — possible
conditions.plain_language: RSV can look like a cold. It can be more serious in babies, older adults, and people with certain health conditions.
useful_follow_up_questions: What is the person's age?
Is breathing fast or difficult?
Is feeding or drinking reduced?
Any chronic lung/heart condition or immune suppression?
do_not_assume: Symptoms cannot confirm RSV without appropriate testing.
Breathing difficulty in infants needs prompt assessment.
red_flags_or_escalation: Use general safety signs; for infants, breathing difficulty, poor feeding, or unusual inactivity needs urgent clinical assessment.

references.title: CDC — Symptoms and Care of RSV

conditions.plain_language: A stomach or intestinal infection can cause diarrhoea, vomiting, nausea, and stomach cramps. Not all gastroenteritis is viral.
useful_follow_up_questions: How often are vomiting or diarrhoea occurring?
Can the person keep fluids down?
Any blood in stool or vomit?
Any severe abdominal pain or reduced urination?
How old is the person?
do_not_assume: Do not label every episode of diarrhoea as viral.
Foodborne illness and other causes may need assessment.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: oral rehydration guidance reviewed for the intended age group
hand hygiene and avoiding food preparation for others while infectious
red_flags_or_escalation: Urgent assessment for blood, severe pain, severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, or inability to keep fluids down.

conditions.plain_language: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection that may cause fever, strong headache, pain behind the eyes, body or joint pain, nausea, or rash. It can become serious and needs local clinical guidance.
symptoms_that_may_fit: relevant local outbreak or mosquito exposure
useful_follow_up_questions: Which day of fever is this?
Any severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, unusual weakness, or cold/pale skin?
Any known local dengue activity or mosquito exposure?
Has a clinician recommended testing?
do_not_assume: Do not diagnose dengue from symptoms alone.
Fever may have other causes, including illnesses requiring different treatment.
A drop in fever does not always mean dengue is improving.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: seek appropriate medical assessment when dengue is plausible
red_flags_or_escalation: Urgent care for severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, rapid breathing, unusual restlessness or marked fatigue, blood in vomit/stool, or pale/cold skin.

conditions.plain_language: Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral infection often associated with fever and prominent joint pain. Symptoms overlap with dengue and other infections.
symptoms_that_may_fit: relevant local outbreak or mosquito exposure
useful_follow_up_questions: How severe is the joint pain and does it limit movement?
Any rash, bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or persistent vomiting?
Any local outbreak or mosquito exposure?
Has a clinician assessed the fever?
do_not_assume: Symptoms alone cannot reliably distinguish chikungunya from dengue.
Do not use a common-condition match to bypass fever assessment.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: avoid medication advice unless reviewed for dengue overlap
red_flags_or_escalation: Use general safety signs and urgent dengue warning signs when relevant.

conditions.display_name: Hand, foot and mouth disease — possible
conditions.plain_language: A contagious viral illness, most common in young children, that may cause fever, painful mouth sores, and a rash on hands and feet.
symptoms_that_may_fit: rash or small blisters on palms/soles
useful_follow_up_questions: What is the person's age?
Can they drink enough fluids?
Are mouth sores preventing drinking?
Is the person unusually sleepy or getting worse?
do_not_assume: Other illnesses can cause rashes or mouth sores.
A rash pattern should not be treated as confirmation.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: avoid close contact according to local guidance
red_flags_or_escalation: Clinical advice if unable to drink, signs of dehydration, persistent high fever, severe symptoms, or worsening condition.

references.title: CDC — Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease

conditions.plain_language: Chickenpox can cause an itchy blister-like rash and fever. It can be more serious in adults, pregnant people, newborns, and people with weakened immune systems.
useful_follow_up_questions: Is the rash blister-like and spreading?
Is the person pregnant, a newborn, an adult, or immunocompromised?
Any eye involvement, breathing problems, or severe illness?
do_not_assume: Many rashes look alike; clinical assessment may be needed.
Avoid contact with high-risk people while seeking advice.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: contact a clinician for diagnosis and isolation advice
red_flags_or_escalation: Prompt assessment for high-risk people, severe symptoms, breathing difficulty, confusion, or rash involving the eyes.

conditions.plain_language: Shingles can cause pain, tingling, and a blistering rash, often in a band on one side of the body. Early medical advice can matter.
symptoms_that_may_fit: burning or tingling pain in one area
useful_follow_up_questions: When did pain and rash begin?
Is the rash near an eye or on the face?
Is the person immunocompromised?
Has a clinician assessed it?
do_not_assume: Other skin conditions can resemble shingles.
Do not delay advice for a rash near the eye.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: cover rash and avoid exposing susceptible high-risk contacts according to clinician guidance
red_flags_or_escalation: Urgent medical advice for rash near the eye/face, immune suppression, widespread rash, or severe illness.

conditions.plain_language: A viral eye infection can cause a watery, irritated or red eye and may spread easily. Eye pain or changes in vision need prompt assessment.
useful_follow_up_questions: Is there eye pain, light sensitivity, or blurred/reduced vision?
Any contact-lens use?
Any injury or chemical exposure?
Is discharge thick or symptoms worsening?
do_not_assume: Not all red eyes are viral.
Eye pain, light sensitivity, or vision changes should not be dismissed.
red_flags_or_escalation: Prompt assessment for eye pain, light sensitivity, vision change, contact-lens-related red eye, injury, or severe symptoms.

conditions.display_name: Sore throat — often viral, cause uncertain
conditions.plain_language: A sore throat often occurs with viral respiratory infections, but other causes are possible. The symptom alone does not identify the cause.
useful_follow_up_questions: Can the person swallow liquids and saliva?
Any difficulty breathing, drooling, or rapidly worsening swelling?
How long has it lasted?
Any rash or severe illness?
do_not_assume: Do not automatically label it viral.
Do not recommend antibiotics without appropriate clinical evaluation.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: clinician/pharmacist advice for symptom relief appropriate to age and health history
red_flags_or_escalation: Urgent help for breathing difficulty, inability to swallow saliva, severe dehydration, or rapidly worsening symptoms.

conditions.plain_language: Fever is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Many infections and some non-infectious conditions can cause it. More information or clinical assessment may be needed.
useful_follow_up_questions: What is the measured temperature and how was it taken?
How many days has fever lasted?
Any cough, sore throat, rash, severe headache, pain, vomiting, diarrhoea, or urinary symptoms?
Any travel, mosquito exposure, pregnancy, immune suppression, or chronic illness?
Any warning signs or rapid worsening?
do_not_assume: Never convert fever alone into a confirmed 'viral fever'.
In regions where dengue or malaria occurs, fever may require specific clinical evaluation.
Do not let a common viral label override warning signs.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: seek clinical advice based on severity, duration, risk factors, and local guidance
red_flags_or_escalation: Fever with severe illness, breathing difficulty, confusion, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, persistent vomiting, or rapid worsening requires urgent assessment.

references.title: CDC — Manage Common Cold (when to seek care)

conditions.plain_language: Allergies can cause sneezing, itchy eyes/nose, and a runny nose, often without fever. This can resemble a cold.
useful_follow_up_questions: Are the eyes or nose itchy?
Do symptoms recur with dust, pollen, pets, or another trigger?
Is fever present?
Any breathing difficulty or swelling of lips/tongue?
do_not_assume: Absence of reported fever is not proof of allergy.
Severe breathing difficulty or face/tongue swelling is an emergency.
routine_guidance_topics_for_review: ask a pharmacist or clinician about appropriate treatment
red_flags_or_escalation: Emergency care for breathing difficulty or swelling of the tongue/throat.

implementation_contract.suggested_use: Load this as a reviewed knowledge/reference layer for Everyday User mode. Use it to guide symptom summaries, follow-up questions, plain-language explanations, and references. Do not use it as a diagnosis engine.
ranking_policy: Do not add arbitrary boosts because a condition is common.
Do not assign percentages from symptom overlap or text similarity.
Do not replace the existing classifier output silently.
If the existing model and reviewed evidence layer disagree, show uncertainty and route for more information or appropriate care rather than force a winner.
Always run the approved safety layer before routine self-care recommendations.
testing_required: Common cold-like symptoms with no warning signs
Fever plus mosquito exposure in an endemic setting
Fever plus severe abdominal pain or bleeding
User says they do NOT have a symptom (negation)
Child, pregnancy, older adult, immunocompromised, and chronic illness scenarios
No matching evidence / low confidence / conflicting evidence
implementation_contract.release_gate: Do not use for real patient triage until qualified clinicians have reviewed condition content, local escalation rules, data handling, and evaluation results.
